subject: Re: Encord/Tau Robotics - Services for G1_Mobile Project
text:
Hi Dave,

I’ve reviewed 7 episodes — overall, they’re quite good. There were only one
or two scores I would adjust by more than 2 points.
My main feedback points are:

   - The humanoid still walks quite slowly and loudly, so it generally
   cannot reach a score of 4 (“good”). If it successfully navigates to the
   target, it usually deserves a 3 (“ok”).
   - When the humanoid touches or bumps into objects, it often applies
   excessive force — for example, pushing against a shelf or grasping the
   cookies too tightly.
   - It should start executing the task promptly once the instruction
   begins. A customer shouldn’t have to wait 10 seconds before it moves.

Some variation is inevitable, but please aim to make scores as
deterministic and reproducible as possible. Try to rate as an average human
evaluator would if told:
“You’ve bought this humanoid and given it these task instructions. How
happy are you with its execution?”
Later, we may have multiple annotators label the same episodes to further
calibrate consistency.

Best,
Alex

   - *Prospect:* Nuffield Health, specifically the fitness and wellness
   part of the business

      - This is a real opportunity with Nuffield Health that I closed
      whilst at DataRobot for over $800k total contract value
      - Cold call was with Ben, first discovery call included Ben and one
      of his analysts (Aidan).

      was blocking AI success was understood enough to indicate that DataRobot
      could solve it. Also, it was explained that currently there is
exec support

      to complete the preparation. He agreed to bring in Alex (Head of Trading)

      - Our call on Fri 31st is the call that includes Alex Alavoine.

I will provide an agenda for the Friday call tomorrow. The aim of the call
is to understand the business urgency to solving the churn problem, which
is required to support aligning a senior Data Scientist in DataRobot to
prepare and present a churn use case demonstration of the solution.

subject: Knock best practice
text:
Hi Carl,

Thanks for the time yesterday as discussed I am not surprised the chat widget didn't deliver many chat as people used to it being a bot and much more of a support solution and don't click on it for buying reasons.

From our experience and best practices adding a CTA will drive 73% higher engagement. 

The top locations where you can see the impact are:

• 

Top navigation - next to the book a demo.

• 

Footer - especially in Encord case where most clicks are on contact us in the footer. 

• 

Pricing page - in the enterprise tier where you need to book a demo to understand pricing, leads prefer to chat and ask questions before booking time. 

As mentioned we are happy to extend the trial in 2 months to make sure you see the value before you need to pay when adding the CTAs. I strongly believe that adding such CTAs in these main locations, will drive more engagement and with that conversions.

Please let me know if you would like me to share examples to how customers added such CTAs in different locations.

Best,

Alon 

 Hate emails, lets move to chat

 Alon Rosenberg

 Co-founder & CEO
